status: Historical context for an explicitly conditional p215 editorial reading.

edition.title: Von Brest-Litovsk zur deutschen Novemberrevolution: Aus den Tagebuechern, Briefen und Aufzeichnungen von Alfons Paquet, Wilhelm Groener und Albert Hopman, Maerz bis November 1918
edition.note: The dated primary texts and the 1971 editor's explanatory notes are identified separately below. The page images are linked, not redistributed.

reviewed_evidence.source_kind: Contemporaneous official directive reproduced in the edition
reviewed_evidence.document_title: Richtlinien fuer die Taetigkeit der Kaiserlichen Marine in der Ukraine und Krim
reviewed_evidence.finding: Item 4 identifies General Kosch as the German commander in Crimea and places the proposed Marineabteilung Krim under him tactically and organizationally.
reviewed_evidence.limit: This establishes the person and command context, not the letters of p215.

reviewed_evidence.source_kind: 1971 editorial biographical annotation, not a contemporary document
reviewed_evidence.finding: The editor identifies Robert Kosch as leader of General Command 52 from August 1916 until the end of the war.
reviewed_evidence.limit: This is editorial identification; it does not decode the final literal reference 3Y52.

reviewed_evidence.source_kind: Albert Hopman's contemporaneous diary as edited in 1971
reviewed_evidence.finding: Kosch and Engelien visit from Simferopol to discuss evacuating the 15th Landwehr Division by sea.
reviewed_evidence.limit: This is a German evacuation discussion, not evidence for the p215 report's two Allied divisions.

reviewed_evidence.source_kind: Albert Hopman's contemporaneous diary as edited in 1971
reviewed_evidence.finding: The diary records GK 52 asking whether the mine barrage had been cleared.
reviewed_evidence.limit: This shows relevant command activity shortly before p215's intercepted date; it is not a parallel transmission.

reviewed_evidence.source_kind: Albert Hopman's contemporaneous diary as edited in 1971
reviewed_evidence.finding: At 08:00 Hopman receives notice from the Allied admirals at Constantinople: a British cruiser with destroyers is expected on Sunday and an Allied squadron on Tuesday.
reviewed_evidence.date_interpretation: Within the dated diary entry, these are 24 and 26 November 1918.
reviewed_evidence.limit: The entry describes expected naval arrivals at Sevastopol; it neither quotes p215 nor confirms its troop composition.

allied_fleet_order.source_kind: Digitized contemporary memorandum copy and enclosure
allied_fleet_order.collection: Papers of Cyril John Percy Hill
allied_fleet_order.item_title: Instructions for the conduct of the Allied fleet proceeding to Sevastopol
allied_fleet_order.transcription_status_at_review: Awaiting approval; original images checked for the stated facts.
findings: The main Allied fleet is to leave Constantinople for Sevastopol on 25 November.
Canterbury, Northesk and Bisson are recorded as having left on 23 November; Adamant and E.21 are to meet the fleet on 26 November.
Enclosure 1 organizes the destroyers in two divisions.
limits: This later order supplies independent naval context and supports the broad arrival chronology relevant to p217.
It does not establish that p215's Divisionen refers to destroyers.
It does not confirm any New Zealand landing or the composition of the p215 report's proposed divisions.

official_diary_fulltext_search.finding: Kosch and GK 52 contexts were identified. No independently corroborating two-divisions/New Zealanders passage was found in the reviewed diary material.
official_diary_fulltext_search.limit: Search depends on spelling, OCR and the edition's selection; no claim of absence from the full archival record is made.

childs_ocr_corpus.finding: No new source-verified p215 retransmission or expansion of MI?I5 was found. The MILI5 hit on p209 is embedded in unrelated garble under an undated key and is rejected as contextual support.
childs_ocr_corpus.limit: The search uses unverified OCR and bounded group/tail hypotheses; the p215 two-missing-group geometry itself is outside that retrieval model.
childs_ocr_corpus.status: Historical search retained by archival URL; the unused retrieval queue and runner are retired from the current tree.
